events.title: Jerusalem regained by treaty during the Sixth Crusade
events.description: Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II signed a ten-year truce with the Ayyubid sultan al-Kamil. It returned Jerusalem, Nazareth and Bethlehem to Christian control without a major battle.
events.significance: It showed that diplomacy could succeed where warfare had failed, and it was one of the most notable negotiated outcomes of the Crusades.

events.title: Duke of Clarence executed in the Tower of London
events.description: George Plantagenet, Duke of Clarence, was put to death after being convicted of treason against his older brother, King Edward IV of England. Tradition says he was drowned in a barrel of wine.
events.significance: The fall of Clarence is among the most notorious episodes of the Wars of the Roses. It later fed the legend of Richard III and Shakespeare's portrayal of the family's bloody rivalries.

events.title: Jefferson Davis inaugurated as Confederate president
events.description: In Montgomery, Alabama, Jefferson Davis was sworn in as provisional President of the Confederate States of America. This came only weeks before Abraham Lincoln took office in Washington.
events.significance: The inauguration gave the breakaway Confederacy a formal leader and government, and it set the stage for the outbreak of the American Civil War in April 1861.

events.title: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn published in the United States
events.description: Mark Twain's novel about a boy and an escaped slave traveling down the Mississippi River was published in the United States. It had appeared in Britain earlier.
events.significance: Often called one of the great American novels, it helped establish a distinctly American voice in literature and continues to spark debate about race and society.
